name: DSSarl Upgrade Scanner for PHP Compatibility
author: Digital Services SARL

sections.description:
Your host wants you on a newer PHP version. Will your plugins and themes keep working?

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner for PHP Compatibility helps you prepare. It reads the PHP code of your plugins and themes and flags code that is likely to break, or is deprecated, on the PHP version you choose. You get a static analysis report organised by plugin or theme, then by file and line, so you (or your developer) know where to look before you switch.

Everything runs on your own server. There is no outside service, no account, no API key, and your code is never sent anywhere. Because the scan is local, it also covers premium and custom plugins and themes that are not on WordPress.org.

How it works

  1. Go to Tools → DSSarl Upgrade Scanner (administrators only).
  2. Pick the PHP version you plan to move to. Released PHP versions are offered (PHP 7.0 to 8.5, plus PHP 8.6 as a preview), and you check against one exact version, so you are not flooded with alerts about PHP versions that do not exist yet.
  3. Pick the plugins and themes to scan. Your active plugins and theme are selected by default.
  4. Click Scan. A progress bar shows the scan running in short batches. Cancel scan stops it at any time.
  5. Read the results: errors first, then warnings, grouped by plugin or theme, then by rule and by file and line.

Built for shared hosting

  • The scan runs in short, resumable batches, so it fits within typical shared-hosting time limits.
  • Large files get their own batch.
  • A file too large for your server’s memory is reported as “Skipped: too large for this server’s memory limit” instead of stopping the scan.
  • Close the tab and the scan continues in the background (more slowly, using WordPress cron, which runs when your site has visits). Come back later to see the results.
  • Cancel at any time.

Clear, usable results

  • Errors – code that is likely to stop working on the chosen PHP version.
  • Warnings – code that is deprecated or may break in a later PHP version.
  • Each finding shows the file, the line and the rule that flagged it.
  • An “update available” hint appears next to plugins and themes that already have an update waiting. Updating first often removes many findings.
  • Ignore a rule or a whole file you have already reviewed.
  • Third-party and development code (for example vendor and tests folders) is labelled and can be hidden, so you can focus on code that actually runs.
  • Common false positives in template files are filtered out.
  • Every report shows the version of the ruleset used, so you know what the scan was based on.
  • Download CSV saves the findings of the latest scan as a spreadsheet file for your developer or your records. Ignored findings are left out, and files that could not be scanned are listed with the reason. The file is created on your server and downloaded by your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

What it does not do

  • It does not change any file.
  • It does not change your PHP version.
  • It does not fix code. It shows you where to look.
  • It is a static analysis tool: it reads code, it does not run it. Some problems only show up at run time and cannot be detected this way. Use the report together with a test on a staging site.

Features

  • Scan plugins and themes against one released PHP version (PHP 7.0 to 8.5, plus PHP 8.6 as a preview)
  • Local scan: no external service, no account, no API key, no data sent
  • Works with premium and custom plugins and themes
  • Resumable background batches with progress bar, designed for shared hosting limits
  • Memory guard: oversized files are skipped and reported, not crashed on
  • Errors vs warnings, by plugin/theme, file, line and rule
  • “Update available” hint
  • Ignore list for rules and files
  • Vendor and test code labelled and hideable
  • Template false positives filtered
  • Ruleset version shown in every report
  • CSV download of the results (UTF-8, for spreadsheet apps)
  • Read-only: never edits your files

Powered by open-source tools

The scan engine uses the open-source PHP_CodeSniffer and PHPCompatibility projects. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner is an independent plugin by Digital Services SARL and is not affiliated with those projects. See “Credits / Third-party libraries” below.

About coverage

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner 1.1.1 uses PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha3, a pre-release. It flags many known changes in recent PHP versions, but coverage of the newest PHP versions is not yet complete. A clean report means no known issue was flagged by the current rules; it is not a guarantee. We update the ruleset when new upstream releases are available.

Trademarks

PHP is a project of The PHP Group. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner for PHP Compatibility is an independent product of DIGITAL SERVICES – SARL and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by The PHP Group or the PHP project.

Disclaimer

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner uses static analysis: it reads the PHP files of your installed plugins and themes without running them, and compares them with the PHPCompatibility rulesets for PHP_CodeSniffer. The PHP 8 rules come from pre-release versions of those rulesets (PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha3); the exact rules version is shown in every report.

Results are guidance only, not a guarantee:

  • Static analysis can report issues that are not real problems (false positives).
  • It can miss issues that appear only when code runs, such as dynamically built code, code loaded from outside the scanned folders, encoded or obfuscated files, server configuration or missing PHP extensions (false negatives).
  • Files that are too large for your server’s memory limit are skipped, and the report says so.
  • A report with no errors does not guarantee that your site will work on a given PHP version.

Always make a full backup and test on a staging site before you change your PHP version or update plugins or themes.

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner never changes your PHP version and never edits your files.

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner is free software, provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind, as stated in the GNU General Public License. To the extent permitted by applicable law, DIGITAL SERVICES – SARL is not liable for downtime, data loss or any other damage arising from the use of the plugin or from decisions made on the basis of its results.

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner is developed by DIGITAL SERVICES – SARL. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the PHP_CodeSniffer or PHPCompatibility projects, The PHP Group or WordPress.org. Credits and licences for the bundled open-source components are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

Credits / Third-party libraries

DSSarl Upgrade Scanner bundles the following open-source projects. Full licence texts and copyright notices are in the THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt file included with the plugin.

  • PHP_CodeSniffer – https://github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer

  • PHPCompatibility – https://github.com/PHPCompatibility/PHPCompatibility
  • PHPCompatibilityWP – https://github.com/PHPCompatibility/PHPCompatibilityWP
  • PHPCompatibilityParagonie – https://github.com/PHPCompatibility/PHPCompatibilityParagonie

sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “DSSarl Upgrade Scanner” and click Install Now, then Activate.
    Or upload the dssarl-upgrade-scanner folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Go to Tools → DSSarl Upgrade Scanner.
  3. Choose your target PHP version, choose the plugins and themes to scan, and click Scan.

Tip: run the scan before you change the PHP version in your hosting panel, and test the change on a staging copy of your site if your host offers one.
sections.faq:
Which PHP versions can I check against?

Only released PHP versions are offered: PHP 7.0 to 8.5, and PHP 8.6 (released in November 2026) as a preview. PHP 8.6 is marked “preview” because the bundled rules for it are not complete yet, so an 8.6 scan may miss some 8.6 issues and a clean 8.6 result does not mean your code is ready for 8.6; the results screen says so after an 8.6 scan. PHP 8.6 is never the default target. PHP versions that have not been released are never offered. You check against one exact version at a time; pick the version your host will move you to.

Does it send my code or site data anywhere?

No. The scan runs entirely on your own server. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner does not call any external service, needs no account or API key, and sends no code or site data anywhere.

Does it work with premium or custom plugins and themes?

Yes. Because the scan reads the files on your own server, it covers premium plugins, custom themes and any other code installed on the site, not only items from WordPress.org.

Why do I see a warning on a plugin that works fine today?

Warnings usually mean the code uses something that is deprecated: it still works on the version you chose but may stop working in a later PHP version. Some findings may also be in code that never runs on your site (for example a fallback for old PHP versions or a third-party library). Check whether an update is available, then ask the plugin author if you are unsure.

What is the difference between an error and a warning?

An error means the code is likely to break on the PHP version you chose. A warning means the code is deprecated or may break in a later version. Look at errors first.

What does “Skipped: too large for this server’s memory limit” mean?

The file was too large to analyse within your server’s memory limit, so DSSarl Upgrade Scanner skipped it instead of stopping the scan. The rest of the results are still valid. You can ask your host for a higher PHP memory limit and scan again, or ask the plugin author about that file.

Can I export the results?

Yes. Below the results, click Download CSV. You get one row per finding with the plugin or theme, its version, the file, line, severity, rule and message, plus the target PHP version, the scan date and the rules version. Findings you have chosen to ignore are left out, files that could not be scanned are included with the reason, and plugins or themes without findings are listed too. The download is limited to administrators (super admins on multisite). The file is created on your server and downloaded by your browser; nothing is sent anywhere, and the plugin does not keep a copy. Keep the file somewhere safe, as it lists the plugins and themes on your site and their versions.

Does it fix the problems it finds?

No. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner never edits files. It shows the plugin or theme, file, line and rule so you can update the plugin, contact its author, or ask a developer to fix it.

Does it change my PHP version?

No. Your PHP version is managed by your host. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner only reads code and reports.

If the report is clean, can I upgrade PHP without any risk?

A clean report means the current rules did not flag any likely incompatibility. It is a helpful check, not a guarantee. Static analysis cannot see everything code does at run time, and coverage of the newest PHP versions is still growing. Always keep a backup and, if possible, test on a staging site first.

Will the scan slow down my site?

The scan runs in short batches in the admin area only, not on the pages your visitors see. On large sites it may take several minutes. You can close the tab, it continues in the background, and you can cancel at any time.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. On a multisite network, only network (super) admins can use it: Tools → DSSarl Upgrade Scanner appears on the main site only. Plugin and theme files are shared by the whole network, so one scan covers the network’s plugins and themes. Results and settings are stored on the main site only, and uninstalling the plugin removes them from every site of the network.

Why are some files labelled “vendor” or “tests”?

These are third-party libraries or development files bundled inside a plugin or theme. They often contain code for many PHP versions or code that never runs on a live site. They are labelled so you can hide them and focus on the code that matters.

Privacy

Privacy: scanning runs entirely on your own server. DSSarl Upgrade Scanner does not send your code, files, scan results or any other site data anywhere.

Scan results are stored in your site’s own database (the latest scan only) and are deleted when you uninstall the plugin.

Administrators can download the latest results as a CSV file. It lists your plugins and themes with their versions, file paths, line numbers and findings, but no visitor or user data and no passwords. The file is created on your server and goes straight to your browser; DSSarl Upgrade Scanner does not keep a copy or send it anywhere. Once downloaded, the file is yours to manage: treat it like other information about your site, because a list of plugins and versions can be useful to an attacker.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Renamed from “Upgrade Checker – PHP Compatibility Scanner” to “DSSarl Upgrade Scanner for PHP Compatibility” (slug and text domain dssarl-upgrade-scanner), the first version submitted under the new name. Translations now come from translate.wordpress.org instead of bundled files.
  • Fix: on phones, the rule code in the “By rule” and file tables is shown on its own line under the message, instead of wrapping letter by letter in a narrow column.
  • Updated the bundled PHPCompatibilityWP (3.0.0-alpha3) and PHPCompatibilityParagonie (2.0.0-alpha3) rulesets. PHPCompatibility is unchanged (10.0.0-alpha3).
  • Readme: the multisite FAQ now describes who can use the plugin on a network and where results are stored.

1.1.0

  • New: Download CSV button on the results screen. One row per finding (plugin or theme, version, file, line, severity, rule, message, third-party/dev code), with the scan date, target PHP version and rules version. Ignored findings are left out; files that could not be scanned are listed with the reason. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so spreadsheet apps such as Excel read accented and Arabic text as UTF-8. Cells that a spreadsheet could read as a formula are written as text.
  • New: PHP 8.6 (preview) target. Rules for PHP 8.6 are not complete yet, so some 8.6 issues may be missed; the results screen and the CSV mark 8.6 scans as a preview. Never the default target.
  • Fix: a cancelled or unfinished scan no longer shows “no likely issues found” for plugins or themes it did not finish; they are marked “not finished”, as in the CSV.
  • Fix: on phones, the results tables scroll inside the screen instead of widening the whole admin page.
  • Fix: multisite – only the main site creates the results table and settings, and uninstall now removes them from every site of the network. When network-activated, the bundled French and Arabic translations are now loaded.
  • Fix: no PHP warning when “Cancel” is sent before any scan exists.
  • Ruleset unchanged: PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha3.

1.0.0

  • First release.
  • Scan plugins and themes against a chosen released PHP version (up to PHP 8.5).
  • Local, resumable background scanning with progress bar and cancel.
  • Memory guard: oversized files reported as skipped.
  • Results by plugin/theme, file, line and rule, with errors and warnings.
  • “Update available” hint, ignore list, vendor/test code labelling, template false-positive filtering.
  • Memory guard estimates each file from its code (tokens) as well as its size, so that dense files are skipped and reported on 128–256 MB servers instead of running out of memory.
  • On PHP 7.2 servers, files using PHP 7.3+ flexible heredoc/nowdoc syntax are listed as “Not scanned” with the reason, instead of producing false errors.
  • “Ignore this file” is offered on files with findings (not on files that could not be scanned, where it would have no effect).
  • Ruleset: PHPCompatibility 10.0.0-alpha3.

screenshots.caption: Choose the target PHP version and the plugins and themes to scan.
Scan in progress: a progress bar with the file count. You can leave the page (the scan continues in the background, more slowly) or cancel the scan.
Results summary: errors, warnings, files not scanned and files scanned for each plugin or theme, with the target PHP version, the rules version used and the disclaimer.
Findings for one plugin, by rule (example message and count, with "Ignore this rule everywhere" or only for this plugin) and by file, with third-party and development code labelled.
